idiom_name: no realization - types over the same libuv event loop; worker_threads for CPU-bound work only
alternative: async/await over the runtime event loop, a bounded worker_threads pool for CPU-bound tasks, and cluster/process-per-core for multi-core accept spreading - the type system cannot make a shared handle set available
implementation_notes: TypeScript shares JavaScript's runtime and inherits its constraint: libuv ties a loop to a single thread, documents that loops and handles are not thread-safe, and performs network I/O on that thread, so the demultiplexing leader cannot be rotated over a shared handle set. Node's worker_threads documentation says workers "do not help much with I/O-intensive work" because the built-in asynchronous I/O is more efficient, and no API moves a listening socket or a connection into another thread's poller: messages and transferable/shared ArrayBuffers are the only cross-thread channels. Types describe the protocol of a worker pool; they cannot type a handle set into existence.
pitfalls: The only state a worker shares is memory you explicitly transfer or share, so a Map<Socket, Handler> is meaningless across threads - a shared handle set cannot be expressed even with types.
Blocking APIs (readFileSync, execSync, synchronous crypto) halt every request on the loop and no other thread can take over the leader role.
Spawning a Worker per task costs more than the work itself; the documentation recommends a bounded pool, with AsyncResource used to correlate tasks for diagnostics.
Compilation does not change the model: a bundler or tsconfig target gives newer syntax, not threads or shareable handles.
